title: incident-exercise-syllabus-and-runbook-retirement-plan-2026
author: Maya Patel
content:
Purpose
-------
This document defines a repeatable syllabus for incident response exercises (game days), the lifecycle policy for runbooks (creation, review, deprecation, retirement), and a set of customer-communication templates tied to the incident lifecycle. The goal is to improve on-call preparedness, keep runbooks accurate and discoverable, and ensure consistent, low-friction customer communications during incidents.

Scope
-----
Applies to all Redwood-hosted services and the teams that own them. This covers: production incidents (P0-P2), scheduled failover drills, tabletop exercises, and any runbook updates or retirements for services with a PagerDuty (or equivalent) escalation. Does not cover purely experimental/local developer environments.

Key definitions
---------------
- Severity definitions (short):
  - P0: Production-wide outage or data-loss affecting multiple customers or core functionality.
  - P1: Major degradation for many customers or key business flows, partial mitigation available.
  - P2: Single-customer outage or degraded non-critical flows.
- Game day types:
  - Tabletop: Discussion-based scenario run with on-call and stakeholders.
  - Live failover: Controlled, hands-on failover of a service / region.
  - Chaos/latency sim: Inject latency/errors to validate SLOs and resilience.

Roles & responsibilities
-------------------------
- Incident Lead (IL): Runs the incident room, makes PB/rollback decisions, coordinates cross-team activity.
- Communications Lead (CL): Owns external status page updates, internal Slack/Email comms, and customer liaison.
- On-call Eng: Performs initial triage, follows runbooks, and implements mitigations.
- Service Owner: Approves runbook changes, signs off on runbook retirement, and prioritizes engineering work.
- SRE Game-day Coordinator: Schedules exercises, publishes post-exercise reports and success criteria.

Runbook lifecycle policy (single-line fields for automation)
-----------------------------------------------------------
1) Creation: New runbook created in Confluence under the service page. Include: overview, pre-requisites, required access, exact CLI/console steps, expected metrics, rollback steps, and test steps. Add label: "runbook-<service>".
2) Ownership: Every runbook must have a single owner (person) and an owning team (team). Owner is accountable for updates and exercises.
3) Review cadence: Runbooks tagged as "critical" (associated with P0/P1 playbooks) must be reviewed every 90 days; non-critical runbooks reviewed every 180 days. Review is recorded with a review date and reviewer initials at top of page.
4) Exercise requirement: Any runbook for a customer-facing service with >5% error budget burn in a quarter must be exercised (tabletop or live) within 30 days.
5) Deprecation: If a runbook is replaced by automation or moved under a different service, mark as "deprecated" with replacement link and notify owning team.
6) Retirement criteria: No pages referencing the runbook, zero incidents invoking it in past 12 months, and confirmed by Service Owner. Retirement announcement posted to #sre and the service team.

Runbook metadata checklist (text table)
--------------------------------------
| Field | Required? | Example |
| Service name | yes | inference-gateway |
| Owner | yes | maya.patel@redwood.ai |
| Runbook ID | yes | RB-2026-034 |
| Severity | yes | P0/P1/P2 |
| Last review | yes | 2026-01-31 |
| Linked playbook | optional | incident-command-playbook |

Game day syllabus (quarterly cadence recommended)
------------------------------------------------
Recommended annual cadence per service:
- Critical (SLO critical, P0 risk): 1 live failover + 2 tabletop sessions per year.
- Important: 1 tabletop + 1 chaos sim per year.
- Low-risk: 1 tabletop per year.

Example game day plan (90-minute tabletop)
1) 00:00-00:05 – Convene, objectives, success criteria.
2) 00:05-00:15 – Scenario brief (service context, starting state, injected fault).
3) 00:15-00:35 – Triage & role assignment; identify primary hypothesis and pertinent dashboards.
4) 00:35-00:55 – Execute runbook steps; record actions in shared doc.
5) 00:55-01:10 – Escalations & cross-team coordination simulated; comms drafted.
6) 01:10-01:25 – Recovery or rollback decision; verify system health.
7) 01:25-01:30 – Immediate retrospective + action items.

Game day artifacts to publish
----------------------------
- Event timeline (minute resolution).
- Decisions log (who decided what and why).
- Action items with owners and due dates.
- Post-exercise scorecard vs success criteria (e.g., time-to-detect, time-to-first-action, end-to-end recovery time).

On-call handoff & rotation templates
-----------------------------------
Handoff checklist (to be completed in Slack #oncall-handoffs and pinned to rotation thread):
- Current pager status: active incidents (IDs and short summary).
- Recent oncall notes: mitigations, temporary configs, feature flags toggled.
- Scheduled maintenance windows or upcoming deploys within next 12 hours.
- Tokens/credentials expiring within oncall window.
- Runbooks recently updated (links).
- Known flaky alerts (thresholds and recommended tuning).

Rotation cadence recommendations
- Primary/Secondary weekly rotation for infra-facing teams.
- 7-on/7-off heuristic discouraged for customer-facing teams unless paired with strong overlap and buddy-system.
- Overnight escalation: only one primary at a time; secondary on-call notified for P0s.

Incident process & communications playbook
------------------------------------------
Immediate steps for on-call (first 15 minutes)
1) Acknowledge and identify severity.
2) Create incident doc (Confluence incident template) and log initial hypothesis.
3) Notify Incident Lead if severity >= P1.
4) Communications Lead drafts first customer-facing status (see templates below) and posts to internal comms channel.
5) If P0, open an incident bridge (Zoom/Hangouts) and add IL, CL, service owner, on-call.

Escalation matrix (short)
- 0-10 min: On-call Eng + IL notified.
- 10-30 min: Add Service Owner and SRE Lead.
- 30+ min or inability to mitigate: Exec on-call notified and customer success looped in.

Metrics to capture during incident (minimum)
- Time to acknowledge (TTA)
- Time to first mitigation (TTFM)
- Time to recovery (TTR)
- Number of callback pages / duplicates
- Error budget impact (estimated)

Customer status page & comms templates
-------------------------------------
All external templates must be approved by Communications Lead before posting. Use plain language and set expectations. Replace <> tokens before publishing.

Initial acknowledgement (within 15 minutes for P0/P1)
Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident affecting <service>
Body: We are investigating an issue affecting <service>. Customers may experience <symptoms>. Our on-call team has been engaged and we will provide an update within 30 minutes. For real-time updates visit: <status.redwood.ai/incident-id>.

Periodic update (every 30 minutes)
Subject: Update — <service> incident (ID: <incident-id>)
Body: Current status: <investigating/mitigating/recovering>. Summary of actions taken: <short list>. Next update scheduled at <time>.

Resolution notice (within 60 minutes of mitigation/resolution)
Subject: Resolved — <service> incident (ID: <incident-id>)
Body: The issue affecting <service> has been resolved as of <timestamp (UTC)>. Root cause analysis is underway; a summary will be posted to <link to postmortem> when complete. If you continue to see issues, please contact support@redwood.ai.

Postmortem & blameless review process
-------------------------------------
Procedure (high level):
1) Postmortem doc created within 48 hours of incident resolution using the postmortem template.
2) Owner assigns primary investigator and reviewer.
3) Write timeline, impact, root cause hypothesis, evidence, and remediation plan.
4) Identify contributing factors and systemic fixes.
5) Action items must include owner and due date; items rated by priority and tracked in JIRA.
6) Blameless review meeting within 7 days.
7) Postmortem published to Confluence and linked from the incident ticket; Cx-facing summary drafted by CL if customer impact.

Retrospective success metrics
- Average time from resolution to postmortem publish: <= 72 hours.
- Fraction of action items completed within due date: >= 80%.
- Reduction in recurrence rate for the same incident class after 6 months: target 50% reduction.

Runbook retirement procedure (steps)
----------------------------------
1) Proposal: Service owner files retirement request on runbook page with justification and replacement link.
2) Notification: Automated email to #sre and owning teams; 14-day comment window.
3) Approval: Service Owner and SRE Lead sign off.
4) Archive: Move page to /deprecated and update references.
5) Post-retirement audit: Verify no open incidents referenced the retired runbook for 6 months.
